messages:
olivia_sales: Quick Q — running a short POC with an EU fintech. They asked: can we guarantee that requests and logs stay within the EU for the hosted API? They also want the current sub‑processor list and to understand routing policy (what happens on overload/fallback). any pricing implications for locking to region?

marta_solutions: Short answer: we can strongly prefer EU-only routing but there are caveats depending on plan and model availability. Hosted supports region pinning, dedicated gives stronger guarantees. I can outline options.

junaid_eng: Technical details: routing is policy-driven. We support an X-Region header and tenant routing rules. By default: region preference -> same-region capacity -> compatible fallback (may be other region or model variant). If you must avoid any cross-region processing, Hosted only can’t promise absolute hard block unless we pair with Dedicated or Private where you control network.

junaid_eng: Example header we use in SDKs:```http
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.inference
Authorization: Bearer $KEY
X-Region: eu-west-1
Content-Type: application/json
```

junaid_eng: Note: not all model variants are in every region. For POC we can pin to a model family available in eu-west-1; throughput/latency profile might differ. KV caching and prefix cache live in-region when served from that region.

marta_solutions: Sub‑processor list link: https://redwood-docs.internal/subprocessors (send to customer under NDA if needed). Current EU dataplane uses cloud provider X (eu-west-1) + analytics subprocessor in eu-west-1; however some infra tools' dashboards are US-hosted — we can redact details or provide exceptions in contract.

patrick_re: Pricing note: region pinning on Hosted = no list price delta, but constrained model selection can affect token costs (smaller quantized variants cheaper). For Dedicated we quote reserved capacity (monthly) — for EU-only pools add ~10–15% uplift for isolated capacity if customer needs guaranteed headroom. Exact numbers depend on throughput. I’ll share a POA (ballpark) after we know QPS and model.

olivia_sales: @marta_solutions @junaid_eng can you confirm what we can put in a customer SOC / questionnaire reply about "data residency"? They want a yes/no on "data will not leave the EU".

security_bot: For security questionnaire: we recommend language like: "We route and process customer inference requests within EU regions by default and provide dedicated EU-only deployments for guaranteed in-region processing. For hosted multi-tenant API, fallback behavior may route to compatible variants in other regions if EU capacity is unavailable; customers requiring hard residency should opt for Dedicated or Private deployments." Link: https://redwood.internal/sec-answers/data-residency.

marta_solutions: For POC strategy: 1) Offer hosted EU pin with X-Region for trial. 2) If they require contractual EU-only guarantee, propose a short Dedicated trial (1–3 months) with reserved EU pool. 3) As fallback, offer an on-prem or VPC Private demo if they have strict regulator constraints.

olivia_sales: The customer also asked about how we handle logs/analytics: do logs remain in-region or are they aggregated elsewhere?

junaid_eng: Logs for hosted API are written to region-specific storage buckets for request traces and KV logs. Some aggregated metrics and alerting pipelines are processed by our global telemetry pipeline (we can exclude customer identifiers and send scrubbed aggregates). If they need full in-region logs + KMS with a local CMK, we can enable Dedicated/Private and use their KMS.

patrick_re: Customer asked about price impact for EU-only logs + CMK: that’s typically an add-on + a small infra surcharge. I'll run numbers once we have expected token volume and retention window.

olivia_sales: One blocker: customer legal insists on a list of subprocessors and a routing policy clause in SOW. Who can own the SOW language?

marta_solutions: I can draft SOW language for routing + subprocessor commitments. Will include explicit statement: "Primary processing in EU; fallback behavior described; Dedicated/Private available for hard residency." @patrick_re pls review pricing clause.

patrick_re: I’ll review and add the commercial terms. If they want a hard residency SLA we need to move to Dedicated pricing.

olivia_sales: Action items: 1) marta to draft SOW paragraph + send sanitized subprocessor list (1769460000). 2) junaid to prepare a quick config snippet and a test plan to validate no-egress during POC. 3) patrick to produce ballpark pricing for EU-hosted pin vs Dedicated EU pool.

marta_solutions: Ack. I’ll ping when draft ready.

deploy-bot: Deployment succeeded: eu-west-1 capacity bump applied to hosted pool at 1769460010 :rocket:

olivia_sales: Perfect — I’ll share SOW + test plan with customer tomorrow. Thanks all :thumbsup:
